description_en: Bālakṛṣṇeśvara Mandira was established by Bālakṛṣṇa Bhāro in 1712. This triple-tiered brick temple is an early example of this particular style. Bālakṛṣṇeśvara Mandira is located to the northeast of the Ṭeku Dobhāna, the confluence of the rivers Vāgmatī and Viṣṇumatī. The roof structure is supported by a spherical brick dome. All outward-facing bricks feature embossed images of fourliṅgasand the short form of their donor's name. The temple has suffered from vandalism; several stone sculptures are missing and the northern door's jamb has been removed. The original plinth has been obliterated by the raised road surface and its modern stone paving, whilst the current stone plinth has been placed in an inappropriate location. Cement covers the three-tiered roof of the temple and further traces of cement plaster attest to a recent repair effort.A stone inscription attached to the temple's wall, although badly damaged and missing its top part, records the temple's construction in 1712 CE (NS 832). It was commissioned by Bālakṛṣṇa Bhāro, a resident of Bonde Ṭola. The inscription names the temple area as Dakṣiṇa Bhairava Sthāna (the place of southern Bhairava) which refers to the famous Pacalī Bhaivara Temple (KAT2580). The inscription also mentions that land was bestowed upon theguṭhīof the temple and indicates that acapāḥwas constructed. Currently, no religious activities are observed at the temple.Each of the four openings of the sanctum feature stonetoraṇas.The southern door's typhaneum has a skull above it. A layer of skull motifs can also be found above each of the doors, something which is rarely seen in the temples of the Valley. A stoneśivaliṅgahas been erected at the center of the sanctum, and stone images of Sūrya, Bhagavatī, Garuḍa and their devotees have been placed at the corners of the room. The south-west corner also houses a stone statue of the temple's consecrator Bālakṛṣṇa and his wife Arpūvāni. The word'bāra(la)kṛṣṇa'is inscribed on the stone slab underneath the statues thus identifying them as the donors. A stone statue of Nandī sits in front of the western door, facing theśivaliṅga.
description_ne: ने.सं. ८३२ मा यो मन्दिर कान्तिपुर, वोन्दे टोलका बालकृष्ण भारोले बनाएका हुन् । बालकृष्णले स्थापना गरेको शिवलिङ्ग भएबाट यसलाई ''बालकृष्णेश्वर'' भनिएको हो । मन्दिरमा भएको शिलापत्रमा दक्षिण भैरव स्थानमा यो मन्दिर बनाएको चर्चा परेको छ । कान्तिपुर शहरबाट दक्षिणमा पर्ने भैरव भएकोले पचलि भैरव आसपासको क्षेत्रलाई ''दक्षिण भैरव स्थान'' भनिएको बुझिन्छ । मन्दिर स्थापनासँगै बालकृष्णले मन्दिरका लागि दुई ठाँउका जग्गा पनि दान गरेको कुरा शिलालेखबाट खुल्दछ । हाल मन्दिरसँग सम्बन्धित कुनै गुठी अस्तित्वमा भएको पाइँदैन भने कुनै सांस्कृतिक गतिविधि पनि भए-गरेको देखिँदैन । शिलापत्रमा चपाःको पनि उल्लेख भएबाट सो समय मन्दिरसँग सम्बन्धित चपाः पनि अस्तित्वमा भएको ज्ञात हुन्छ तर हाल मन्दिर परिसरमा कुनै चपाःको अवशेष भेटिँदैन ।शिखर शैलीमा बनेको मन्दिर इँट र ढुङ्गाबाट बनेको छ । मन्दिरको तल्लो भागको प्रत्येक इँटमा शिवलिङ्गको चित्र र बारे(ले)श्वर शब्द अङ्कित छ । गर्भगृह प्रवेश गर्न चौतर्फी ढोकाहरू बनेका छन् । चारै ढोकामाथि कंकालका मुण्डहरू लहरै राखिएको तोरण (tympanum) पाइएको छ । यस प्रकारको कंकाल तोरण उपत्यकाका अन्य मन्दिरमा भएको देखिँदैन । गर्भगृहभित्र ढुङ्गाको शिवलिङ्ग छ भने शिवलिङ्गतिर फर्काई राखिएको नन्दिको मूर्ति पश्चिमी ढोका बाहिर राखिएको छ । गर्भगृहको चारै कुनामा, सूर्य, भगवती, गरुडका साथै भक्तका प्रतिमा कुँदिएको ढुङ्गाका फलकहरू टाँसिएर राखिएका छन् । दक्षिण–पश्चिम कुनामा भने नमस्करण मुद्रामा बसेका बालकृष्ण र उनका पत्नी अर्पूवानिको प्रतिमा एकै ढुङ्गाको फलकमा कुँदी राखिएको छ । यस प्रतिमा फलकमा ''बार(ल)कृष्ण'' शब्द लेखिएबाट यो मूर्ति मन्दिर निर्माता दम्पतीको नै भएको पुष्टि हुन्छ ।

historical_events.event_description: The temple was constructed by Bālakṛṣṇa Bhāro from Vonde Ṭola, during the reign of King Bhāṣkara Malla. Bālakṛṣṇa Bhāro also donated land to provide income for the upkeep of the temple.

The inscription states the name of Bālakṛṣṇeśvara and the date as the full moon day in the month of Vaiśākha, NS 832. The meaning of the inscription is not clear. This date might refer to an unknown event that happened 6 months after the temple was established.Gutschow(2011, 566) interprets this as the date of its consecration.
